newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel says Germany could back big NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel says Germany could back big NATO expansion.

text.p: The German government could support a larger NATO expansion to include four or five new members at the Madrid summit meeting, Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Sunday.
"The decision is still open," Kinkel told the Welt am Sonntag newspaper before the start of the NATO summit in Madrid on Tuesday. "It will be exciting in Madrid."

Kinkel said the U.S. position limiting the enlargement to three nations meant that a final decision has already been made. France and many European nations in NATO want to open the 16-nation alliance to five new members.

Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to be invited to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation at the summit. While the United States wants to limit the first enlargement to those three, many European NATO members want Slovenia and Romania included.

"The (German) government could support a larger enlargement of four or five new members," Kinkel said. "The alliance decisions are always a consensus. Germany's open position is oriented towards finding a consensus."
Kinkel said Germany, which has stayed officially noncommital on the size of the eastern enlargement, was heading to the summit confident that there would be a compromise.
